LESSON: WRITING 13.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Writing 13.4.1 Spelling

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 13.4.1 Spelling
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we write words correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly
2. spell homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly
3. uses homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels in sentences correctly

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 13.4.1 Spelling

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 13.4.1 Spelling

Teach
• Focus skill: identify homophones, words with double consonants and words with double vowels correctly.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 13.4.1 Spelling.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 13.4.1 Spelling
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we write words correctly?
2. Which words have the same pronunciation but different spelling?
3. what went well and why?
4. what did not go well and why?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
